boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Adairsville record (May 17, 1864) in Atlanta Campaign [May-September 1864]. The pursuit from Resaca on May 16 and the Cassville positions of May 18-19 are context outside the frozen date. The live NPS page labels the campaign "Morgan's Raid Into Kentucky" and dates it May-September 1864; neither field replaces the frozen campaign or battle interval. Campaign-wide totals are context and are not assigned to this record. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force fields name the two armies without counts; the live field reads zero. Cox says French's infantry and Jackson's cavalry divisions joined at Adairsville and that from May 15 for a month the two armies were more nearly equal than at any other time in the campaign; his Appendix A gives Jackson's line-of-battle strength from Lee's May 10 return as 405 officers and 4,072 men. Cox says Cheatham's division and Wheeler's cavalry formed the rear guard. Johnston cites the great numerical superiority of the Federal army.
claims.rationale: Army-level and divisional figures on different dates and bases, plus conflicting qualitative judgments; none measures troops engaged on May 17 and none is adopted. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: Cox says the country between the Oostanaula and Etowah was the most open in northern Georgia, that Johnston sought a valley narrow enough to rest both wings on commanding ground, and that at Adairsville the valley was again found too wide; the rear guard fought from barricades of rails and logs. NPS says the valley was too wide, so Johnston disengaged.
claims.rationale: Ground described by an interested history and a summary; no map verification. The valley's width is an inherited feature, but Johnston's choice of ground is his own; no inherited tag is assigned.

claims.value: Johnston says he determined to fall back slowly until circumstances favoured battle, keeping close enough to stop Sherman sending reinforcements to Grant. Cox says Sherman's plan was for the Army of the Cumberland to hold Johnston while a wing attacked his flank or rear, and that at nightfall Sherman hoped for a pitched battle next day. NPS says Sherman concentrated to attack the next day.
claims.rationale: Stated aims from interested accounts and a summary; not a causal estimate.

claims.value: The frozen result is a Confederate delaying action (credited with allowing the Cassville plan); the live page reads Confederate Victory. Cox says Johnston ordered a further retreat to Cassville and that the lines were vacant at daybreak on the 18th. NPS says the 44th Illinois and 24th Wisconsin attacked Cheatham's division at the Saxon (Octagon) house with heavy losses.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. The frozen gloss about Cassville is a later-campaign judgment, not part of the tactical result.

open_questions: Howard's, Newton's and Wood's reports, Hardee's itinerary for May 17, Cleburne's August 16 report (read, not selected) and the compiled returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live battle page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Cox's Atlanta (Scribner, 1882) is a second: a retrospective Union history by the Twenty-third Corps division commander, drawing on official reports and memoirs, so it is not independent of them. Johnston's October 20, 1864 report, printed in Volume XXXVIII Part 3, is a third family (interested Confederate account). Official Records Series I Volume XXXVIII is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting. Campaign-wide strength and loss totals are context, not assigned to one record.
